With vaccinations progressing and policy support in place, the FOMC’s July 28, 2021 decision to keep the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% and continue Treasury and agency MBS purchases remains appropriate for sustaining the recovery and anchoring inflation expectations under average-inflation targeting.

The July 2021 SLOOS points to an improving credit backdrop—stronger C&I loan demand (including at foreign banks), easing terms, and firmer household credit demand—supporting the transmission of accommodative policy.

The July 2021 Beige Book adds incremental confirmation of momentum: reports of increased hiring and rising wages in the New York District, alongside a boost in tourism, suggest continued healing in labor markets and services activity. While wage gains underscore emerging cost pressures, they are consistent with robust demand and improving employment.

Balancing these positives with the Financial Stability Report’s cautions—elevated valuations, high business leverage, nonbank funding vulnerabilities, and sectoral risks in CRE (especially office and lodging)—the outlook remains supportive but measured. On net, Beige Book evidence nudges sentiment modestly higher.
